draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Bandra West! St. Andrew's Church, an 11 min walk away, was built by Portuguese Jesuits in 1575 and is one of the oldest churches in Mumbai. For about half a century it was the only church in Bandra.
draft.hungryLine: Wander down to Pali Market at the foot of Pali Hill, where Jude Bakery has sold bread and eggs for years and restaurants and pubs fill the lanes.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk up Hill Road past St. Peter's Church and the Tata Agiary, then on to St. Andrew's Church by the sea.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Jogger's Park is a seaside park at the southern end of Carter Road, with a 400 m jogging track.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Jogger's Park used to be a dumping ground. Film stars Dilip Kumar and Sunil Dutt helped raise funds to turn it into a park.

spots.name: St. Andrew's Church
spots.detail: 11 min walk · Built in 1575 on the Bandra sea-shore

spots.name: Tata Agiary
spots.detail: 9 min walk · The Tata Parsi agiary from 1873, a Hill Road landmark

spots.name: St. Peter's Church
spots.detail: 7 min walk · Right next to the old St. Stanislaus school on Hill Road

legends.title: The salty village
legends.body: Next-door Khar gets its name from khāra, Marathi for salty. A couple of centuries ago, locals farmed salt in pans near the Khar Danda shore.

legends.title: A lake with no known owner
legends.body: Locals say this lake was built by an unknown rich Konkani Muslim from nearby Navpada. It was once called Lotus Tank, and also Motha Sarovar.

tips.title: Skip Hill Road on Friday.
tips.body: The shops on Hill Road are closed on Fridays.

tips.title: Know its other name.
tips.body: Hill Road was officially renamed Ramdas Nayak Road, so you may see that on signs.

story.title: The first church
story.body: Portuguese Jesuits built St. Andrew's Church on the Bandra sea-shore. It stayed the only church here until the first quarter of the 17th century.

story.title: Salt and a lake
story.body: Bandra Talao was dug about 200 years ago and spreads over 7.5 acres. Around then, locals also farmed salt near the Khar Danda shore.

story.title: An orphanage becomes a school
story.body: German Jesuit priests started St. Stanislaus as an orphanage. Today it's a boys' school with one of the largest campuses in Mumbai.

story.title: The agiary
story.body: The Tata Parsi agiary went up on Hill Road. It's still one of the road's best-known landmarks.

story.title: From dump to park
story.body: Jogger's Park opened on 27 May 1990 on a former dumping ground. In 2022 the BMC passed a proposal to rename it Sir Oliver Andrade Park, after the hockey coach behind it.
